title: WPSS/1592/2021 of ANIL SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1592 of 2021
Anil Singh ... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ... Respondents
Advocates : Mr. Tarun Prakash Singh Takuli, Advocate, for the petitioner
Mrs. Anjali Bhargava, Addl. CSC, for the State
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The District Education Officer, Primary Education, Pauri
Garhwal, by issuing an Advertisement No. 345 of 2021 dated
10.12.2021, invited applications for making recruitments, as
against 162 vacant posts of the Assistant Teachers Grade-3. As
per the educational qualifications, prescribed therein in the
advertisement, a candidate was expected to have a C.T.E.T.
Examination Certificate in order to make him or her eligible to
apply before the cut off date, which was provided therein as
19.02.2021.
2. The admitted position, which has emerged is that as on the
last date of the submission of application, the petitioner was not
having the minimum required educational qualification as per the
advertisement dated 10.12.2020, because it is an admitted case of
the petitioner, that he has supplied the C.T.E.T. certificate only
on 26.02.2021.
3. There are two limbs of argument of the learned counsel for
the petitioner. Firstly, he submits that in pursuance to the
subsequent advertisement dated 26.09.2021, which he reads it as
if it was an advertisement which was issued by the District
Education Officer, for the purposes of fulfilling the lacuna in the
educational qualification, which stood rectified, according to the

2
petitioner by supplying the documents of his C.T.E.T.
qualification on 26.02.2021, in fact, is contrary to the very
intention of the advertisement dated 26.09.2021, because it only
provided, that whatsoever the tabulations of marks has been done
by the Selecting Body, that could be rectified in case if there is a
wrongful tabulation made, rather it had nowhere provided, that a
candidate would be permitted to supply the documents of the
qualification afresh under the garb of the advertisement dated
26.09.2021 except for the exception of documents which has
been given therein i.e. for the purposes of the experience
certificate, resident certificate and other documents provided
therein, which didn't included within it the certificates pertaining
to minimum educational qualifications required by the
advertisement dated 10.12.2020. Hence, the advertisement dated
26.09.2021, has been wrongly construed by the petitioner, as if it
was enabling him to submit the educational qualification
certificate too to make him eligible to be considered for
appointment in pursuance to the advertisement dated 10.12.2020.
4. Secondly, learned counsel for the petitioner submits, that in
the list thus published by the respondents, they have included the
name of one Manisha, whose name appears at Sl. No. 11. He
submits that inclusion of the name of Manisha, was done despite
the fact that she was not holding the educational qualification and
in that eventuality, the petitioner claims a parity based on the
inclusion of name of Manisha.
5. This Court is not inclined to accede to the said argument
extended by the learned counsel for the petitioner for two
reasons, that if the entries made in column 14 of the said
tabulation made by the District Education Officer, it pertained to
the eligibility of "handicapped eligible candidates", which were

3
included for the purposes of recruitment in the science cadre
which is not the case of the petitioner. The last column provided
and it reads as under:-
**Vh0bZ0Vh0 mRrh.kZ frfFk foKfIr frfFk d s ckn dh gSA vkSic af/kd**
6. In fact, if the entries made as against the name Manisha is
concerned, her result has been kept as 'aupbandhik' due to her
ineligibility of not having the C.T.E.T. certificate on the date of
the submission of the application form. Hence, the reference of
name of Manisha in column 11, as against the handicapped
candidates cannot permit and grant the liberty to the petitioner to
claim a parity, based on the fact that for the reason being, that
petitioner was not falling under the zone for consideration under
the same category of handicapped person, secondly, the result of
Manisha was of 'aupbandhik' due to non providing the eligibility
certificate of having qualified of TET examination and apart from
it no negative parity can be claim by the petitioner to overcome
the conditions of eligibility of qualification provided in the
principal advertisement. Hence, none of the arguments as
extended by the petitioner's counsel for acceptance of his
candidature to be considered for the process of recruitment could
be accepted by this Court.
7. Accordingly, I am not inclined to interfere in the writ
petition; the writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
14.12.2021 Mahinder/
